rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By approving the speaker’s declaration of fear, God depicts him as learned; the Qur’an likewise says that only learned servants fear God and calls Moses’ companion learned.
rows.anchor: فحكايته تعالى قوله { إني أخاف الله رب العالمين } وإمضاؤه له توصيف له بالعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning lays out religion’s foundations: one Lord governs all, people divide into pious and unjust, God loves justice and hates oppression, worship requires piety, wrongdoing incurs liability, and the afterlife repays wrongdoers with hell.
rows.anchor: أصول المعارف الدينية ومجامع علوم المبدأ والمعاد أفاضها هذا العبد الصالح إفاضة ضافية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The text does not say he refused to defend himself; he only says he will not kill first, and may have been attacked by surprise, killed while defending himself, or while evading the attack.
rows.anchor: لم يقل لأخيه حينما كلمه إنك إن أردت أن تقتلني ألقيت نفسي بين يديك ولم أدافع عن نفسي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His willingness to accept the stated consequence applies only if his brother initiates; it does not mean he desired death to secure his own salvation by damning his brother.
rows.anchor: وإنما قال إني أريد ذلك وأختاره على تقدير بسطك يدك لقتلي

words: مَآ أَنَا۠ بِبَاسِطٍۢ يَدِىَ إِلَيْكَ لِأَقْتُلَكَ
rows.speaker: بعض المتقشفين من أهل العبادة والورع
rows.claim: Some ascetics hold that one should passively accept oppression, since the oppressor alone bears its sin; Tabatabai calls this ignorance about complicity in wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: كبعض المتقشفين من أهل العبادة والورع حيث يرى أن الذي عليه هو التزهد والتعبد

words: مَآ أَنَا۠ بِبَاسِطٍۢ يَدِىَ إِلَيْكَ لِأَقْتُلَكَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Helping another commit sin makes both helper and helped share guilt, so the victim’s alleged passivity cannot be justified by saying only the aggressor bears the wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: فإنه من الإعانة على الإثم، وهي توجب اشتراك المعين والمعان في الإثم جميعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cain was so ignorant that he did not know burial could conceal something from view until he learned it from the crow.
rows.anchor: الذي لم يكن يعرف أن الشيء يمكن أن يتوارى عن الأنظار بالدفن حتى تعلمه من الغراب

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Raghib derives bawāʾ from equality of parts in a place and explains tabawwaʾ as settling in a prepared place; interpreting it as returning gives the word’s implication.
rows.anchor: وقال الراغب في مفرداته أصل البواء مساواة الأجزاء في المكان خلاف النبوة الذي هو منافاة الأجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabatabai reads the phrase to mean that the murdered victim’s sin transfers to his killer and joins the killer’s own sin, leaving the victim guiltless; he says reports and reason support this.
rows.anchor: أن ينتقل إثم المقتول ظلما إلى قاتله على إثمه الذي كان له فيجتمع عليه الإثمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although this seems to violate the rule that no bearer carries another’s burden, Tabatabai says that rule concerns practical social judgment, where society may assign liability on recognized grounds.
rows.anchor: مدفوع بأن ذلك ليس من أحكام العقل النظري حتى يختم عليه باستحالة الوقوع، بل من أحكام العقل العملي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Society may collect its rights from a killer or cancel an insurgent’s good deeds; the victim’s sins then count as burdens acquired through the oppressor’s injustice, not as another’s original burden.
rows.anchor: فمن الجائز أن يستوفي المجتمع حقوقه من القاتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sin transferred through a new cause resembles property acquired through sale: the former owner’s rights do not bar the new owner’s possession, and transfer does not nullify the rule against wrongful taking.
rows.anchor: ولا أن قوله { لا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى } يبقى بلا فائدة ولا أثر بسبب جواز انتقال الوزر بسبب جديد

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud, Ibn ʿAbbas, and others are reported to read the two sins as the sin of murdering the speaker, if killed, plus the killer’s earlier sin.
rows.anchor: كما نقل عن ابن مسعود وابن عباس وغيرهما

rows.speaker: الجبائي والزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Jubbaʾi and al-Zajjaj are reported to mean the sin of murdering the speaker plus the sin that caused the killer’s offering to be rejected.
rows.anchor: كما نقل عن الجبائي والزجاج

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Other commentators are reported to understand the speaker’s sin as the sin of killing all people.
rows.anchor: كما نقل عن آخرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabatabai rejects these alternatives: none has linguistic evidence or rational support, and the contrast between two sins both borne by the killer lacks a sound basis.
rows.anchor: وهذه وجوه ذكروها ليس على شيء منها من جهة اللفظ دليل، ولا يساعد عليه اعتبار

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Raghib glosses ṭawʿ as compliance, opposed to compulsion, and says ṭāʿa is similar but usually describes obeying a command or carrying out an order.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب في مفرداته الطوع الانقياد ويضاده الكره، والطاعة مثله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabatabai explains the tafaʿʿul form as gradual yielding, unlike abrupt ifʿāl: repeated whispering and impulses slowly bring the soul to full obedience in the murder.
rows.anchor: فالتطويع في الآية اقتراب تدريجي للنفس من الفعل بوسوسة بعد وسوسة وهمامة بعد همامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this reading, qatla akhīhi places the commanded act where the command would stand, as in saying that someone obeyed an act to mean obeyed its order.
rows.anchor: فقوله { قتل أخيه } من وضع المأمور به موضع الأمر

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: An alternative gloss takes ṭawwaʿat as beautifying the murder, making qatla akhīhi a direct object.
rows.anchor: وربما قيل إن قوله طوعت بمعنى زينت فقوله { قتل أخيه } مفعول به

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another analysis treats the verb as ṭāwaʿat, meaning the soul complied with him in the murder, with qatla accusative after omitting a preposition.
rows.anchor: وقيل بمعنى طاوعت أي طاوعت له نفسه في قتل أخيه، فالقتل منصوب بنزع الخافض

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some infer from aṣbaḥa that Cain killed at night, since aṣbaḥa originally contrasts with amsā; Tabatabai rejects this inference because Arabic commonly uses it to mean became.
rows.anchor: وإن كان بحسب أصل معناه يفيد ذلك لكن عرف العرب يستعمله بمعنى صار

rows.speaker: المجمع
rows.claim: Al-Majmaʿ defines baḥth first as seeking something in the soil, then as searching into a matter.
rows.anchor: البحث طلب الشيء في التراب ثم يقال بحثت عن الأمر بحثا كذا في المجمع.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muwārāt means concealment; tawārī is hiding oneself, and warāʾ denotes what lies behind a thing.
rows.anchor: والمواراة الستر، ومنه التواري للتستر، والوراء لما خلف الشيء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sawʾah is something a person finds repugnant.
rows.anchor: والسوأة ما يتكرهه الإنسان. والويل الهلاك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wayl means destruction, and yā waylatā is an expression uttered in calamity.
rows.anchor: والويل الهلاك. ويا ويلتا كلمة تقال عند الهلكة، والعجز مقابل الاستطاعة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAjz, incapacity, is the opposite of ability.
rows.anchor: ويا ويلتا كلمة تقال عند الهلكة، والعجز مقابل الاستطاعة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The context suggests Cain remained confused for some time, fearing discovery and not knowing how to conceal the body; the exclamation makes little sense if the crow appeared immediately after the killing.
rows.anchor: أن القاتل قد كان بقي زمانا على تحير من أمره، وكان يحذر أن يعلم به غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The crow must have buried something after digging: digging alone would not teach concealment to someone who did not yet understand its relation to burial.
rows.anchor: فإن ظاهر الكلام أن الغراب أراد إراءة كيفية المواراة لا كيفية البحث، ومجرد البحث ما كان يعلمه كيفية المواراة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Crows commonly bury some captured prey for later use; seed-eating birds may search the earth for grains or worms but do not dig to bury and store food.
rows.anchor: والغراب من بين الطير من عادته أنه يدخر بعض ما اصطاده لنفسه بدفنه في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The subject who shows Cain is most naturally the crow, the nearest antecedent, though the meaning remains sound if the pronoun refers to God.
rows.anchor: إلى الغراب هو الظاهر من الكلام لكونه هو المرجع القريب

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative view makes God the subject of the showing; Tabatabai allows it but considers it somewhat remote.
rows.anchor: وربما قيل إن الضمير راجع إلى الله سبحانه، ولا بأس به لكنه لا يخلو عن شيء من البعد

words: أَعَجَزْتُ أَنْ أَكُونَ مِثْلَ هَٰذَا ٱلْغُرَابِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cain saw that he could imitate the crow’s simple digging and use it to conceal the body; his self-address asks rhetorically whether he was unable, then reproaches his failure to think of the obvious means.
rows.anchor: وهو تخاطب جار بينه وبين نفسه على طريق الاستفهام الإنكاري، والتقدير أن يستفهم منكرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Regret is an inward distress caused by recognizing that one neglected an available means and thereby lost a benefit or incurred harm.
rows.anchor: فإن الندامة تأثر روحي خاص من الإنسان وتألم باطني يعرضه من مشاهدته إهماله شيئا من الأسباب المؤدية إلى فوت منفعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wrongdoing violates the community’s interdependent order, whose consequences surface even when initially hidden; the criminal’s effort to force the order to accept it resembles trying to digest poison, while God watches for its due consequence.
rows.anchor: والإنسان الظالم المجرم يريد أن يجبر النظام على قبوله وليس بقابل نظير أن يأكل الإنسان أو يشرب شيئا من السم وهو يريد أن يهضمه جهاز هضمه وليس بهاضم، فهو وإن أمكن وروده في باطنه لكن له موعدا لن يخلفه ومرصدا لن يتجاوزه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A wrongdoer discovers defects in his planning and regrets them; repairing one lapse exposes another, until God finally exposes him before the gathered witnesses.
rows.anchor: ولو عاد فأصلح هذا الواحد فسد آخر ولا يزال الأمر على ذلك حتى يفضحه الله على رؤوس الاشهاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabatabai takes Cain’s regret primarily as regret for failing to bury his brother’s body.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى ندامته على عدم مواراته سوأة أخيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He also allows that Cain may have regretted the murder itself; Tabatabai says this possibility is not far-fetched.
rows.anchor: وربما أمكن أن يقال إن المراد به ندمه على أصل القتل، وليس ببعيد.

words: فَبَعَثَ ٱللَّهُ غُرَابًۭا يَبْحَثُ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This unique Qur’anic episode models learning by sensation: people perceive properties of things and reason from them toward practical aims, supporting the view that human knowledge originates in sense against recollection or innate-knowledge theories.
rows.anchor: آية واحدة في القرآن لا نظيرة لها من نوعها وهي تمثل حال الإنسان في الانتفاع بالحس، وأنه يحصل خواص الأشياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even the most ignorant person possesses an immense, uncountable store of ideas and knowledge that continually grows during earthly life, then diminishes backward toward zero; God taught humanity what it did not know.
rows.anchor: ومن المشهود من أمرها على كثرتها وخروجها عن طور الإحصاء والتعديد أنها لا تزال تزيد وتنمو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The teaching verse does not exempt already acquired knowledge from God’s instruction: all knowledge guides people toward perfection and benefit, just as living beings follow knowledge while nonliving things follow natural impulses.
rows.anchor: وليس المراد بالآية أنه تعالى يعلمه ما لم يعلم وأما ما علمه فهو فيه في غنى عن تعليم ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowledge is a form of guidance: nonliving beings reach their destinations by natural impulses, while living beings, including humans, are guided toward them by the light of knowledge.
rows.anchor: وتهتدي أقسام الموجودات الحية - ومنها الإنسان - إليه بنور العلم فالعلم من مصاديق الهدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God ascribes absolute guidance to himself; Tabatabai uses this to support the claim that human knowledge, as guidance, comes from God.
rows.anchor: وقد نسب الله سبحانه مطلق الهداية إلى نفسه حيث قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since all knowledge is guidance and all guidance comes from God, every human acquisition of knowledge is ultimately by divine teaching.
rows.anchor: وبالجملة لما كان كل علم هداية، وكل هداية فهي من الله كان كل علم للإنسان بتعليمه تعالى

words: فَبَعَثَ ٱللَّهُ غُرَابًۭا يَبْحَثُ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Theoretical knowledge of things and related rational learning begin with sensation; the Qur’an also describes people as emerging from their mothers knowing nothing, then receiving hearing, sight, and hearts.
rows.anchor: أن علم الإنسان النظري أعني العلم بخواص الأشياء وما يستتبعه من المعارف العقلية يبتدئ من الحس فيعلمه الله من طريقه خواص الأشياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s sending the crow to show burial is equivalent to teaching the method; neither crow nor Adam’s son need recognize the divine direction for the event to teach him.
rows.anchor: فنسبة بعث الغراب لإراءة كيفية المواراة إلى الله سبحانه نسبة تعليم كيفية المواراة إليه تعالى بعينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The event may look accidental, but God created people for a life perfected by knowledge and arranged the universe so encounters with its parts teach them how to pursue their aims.
rows.anchor: وكانت سببية الغراب وبحثه بالنسبة إلى تعلمه بحسب النظر الظاهري سببية اتفاقية كسائر الأسباب الاتفاقية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an likewise calls trained hunting animals’ skills knowledge taught by God, although people learned them from others or devised them themselves; those intermediate means remain divine teaching.
rows.anchor: وما علمتم من الجوارح مكلبين تعلمونهن مما علمكم الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an says God teaches people through piety, although they learn these matters from the Messenger; divine instruction works through created means.
rows.anchor: واتقوا الله ويعلمكم الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A scribe may learn from another scribe, yet the Qur’an calls it God’s teaching; in creation and governance, God teaches through causes just as human teachers use speech or a pen.
rows.anchor: فما حصل من هذه الأسباب من فائدة العلم الذي يستكمل به الإنسان فالله سبحانه هو معلمه بهذه الأسباب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God creates through secondary causes that function as apparent means, tools, and conditions; a person’s existence presupposes parents and union, just as sight presupposes a functioning eye.
rows.anchor: وبينه وبين مخلوقه أسباب هي الأسباب بحسب الظاهر وهي أدوات وآلات لوجود الشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who deny causes to magnify divine power and avoid making God seem compelled by necessary means contradict themselves; causality does not negate divine choice.
rows.anchor: فمن زعم أنه يوحد الله سبحانه بنفي الأسباب وإلغائها، وقدر أن ذلك أبلغ في إثبات قدرته المطلقة ونفي العجز عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God teaches properties through the senses and subjugates the heavens and earth for human use, enabling people to think out how to employ them for life’s aims.
rows.anchor: وبالجملة فالله سبحانه هو الذي علم الإنسان خواص الأشياء التي تنالها حواسه نوعا من النيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur’anic language attributes to God the ships humans make, the carrying done by ships and livestock, and their motion through sea, wind, or steam; these are divine subjugation because human will directs them toward desired ends.
rows.anchor: فانظر إلى لسان الآيات كيف نسبت جعل الفلك إلى الله سبحانه وهو من صنع الإنسان، ثم نسب الحمل إليه تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gives humans thought grounded in sensation so theoretical knowledge of the created world can lead them toward their appointed perfection.
rows.anchor: وبالجملة هو سبحانه أعطاه الفكر على الحس ليتوسل به إلى كماله المقدر له بسبب علومه الفكرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Practical knowledge of what ought or ought not be done comes through divine inspiration rather than sensation or theoretical reason; moral good and evil are cast into the heart and disclose innate nature.
rows.anchor: وأما العلوم العملية وهي التي تجري فيما ينبغي أن يعمل وما لا ينبغي فإنما هي بإلهام من الله سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All knowledge is divine guidance, but its means differ: sensory properties come through perception, universal theory through God-given thought, and practical moral judgment through inspiration and the call of innate nature.
rows.anchor: فجميع ما يحصل للإنسان من العلم إنما هي هداية إلهية وبهداية إلهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moral inspiration succeeds when theoretical reason is sound, while reason itself functions properly when a person follows innate religion and piety.
rows.anchor: والقسم الثالث الذي يرجع بحسب الأصل إلى إلهام إلهي إنما ينجح في عمله ويتم في أثره إذا صلح القسم الثاني ونشأ على صحة واستقامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An impaired intellect cannot distinguish truth from falsehood and therefore cannot be guided in moral duties; someone who sees only immediate material life will lack the piety that prepares for the hereafter.
rows.anchor: فإن الإنسان إذا أصيب في قوته النظرية فلم يدرك الحق حقا أو لم يدرك الباطل باطلا فكيف يلهم بلزوم هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Conversely, corrupt innate religion and lack of piety disorder desire, anger, love, and aversion, preventing the theoretical faculty from working well.
rows.anchor: وكذلك الإنسان إذا فسد دينه الفطري ولم يتزود من التقوى الديني لم تعتدل قواه الداخلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an directs perceptible particulars to observation, general or unseen questions to reasoning, and practical questions of good, evil, piety, and sin to inward divine prompting.
rows.anchor: فما كان من الجزئيات التي لها خواص تقبل الإحساس فإنها تسريح فيها إلى الحواس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an corrects empiricists who rely on sense and experiment while denying purely rational judgments in practical inquiry; its first concern is monotheism, on which all true knowledge rests.
rows.anchor: أن القرآن الكريم يخطئ طريق الحسيين وهم المعتمدون على الحس والتجربة، النافون للأحكام العقلية الصرفة في الأبحاث العملية
